name: Aerobic Respiration and Electron Transport
description: Aerobic respiration in E. coli is the energy-generating process that uses oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor, producing significantly more ATP than fermentation. The pathway includes glycolysis, TCA cycle, and a flexible electron transport chain with multiple dehydrogenases and terminal oxidases (bo3, bd-I, bd-II) that adapt to different oxygen concentrations. Regulation involves ArcAB and FNR systems responding to oxygen availability.
